profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review between the project lead and the hardware-facing research engineer for an internal paper proposal on effective compression ratio (ECR) in quantized neural networks under a 256 kbit on-chip SRAM constraint. The proposal compares widening versus lowering weight precision for two existing model families already used in the lab: a 4-layer fully-connected network on Fashion-MNIST and a 9-layer CNN on CIFAR-10. The agenda is to review whether the current experimental plan is solid enough to approve: confirm that the capacity accounting is appropriate for the hardware story, verify that the proposed baselines are the right anchors for the ECR plots, and decide what results are sufficient to call a quantized-or-widened variant 'matched' to the floating-point reference. The expected outcome is approval to proceed with the sweep and a shared sense that the resulting figures will be paper-ready, even though some second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Model compression, efficient deep learning, empirical study design
members.background: Leads an academic ML systems group and has previously published on quantization-aware evaluation for edge deployment; she is reviewing the proposal before the team commits compute time and drafting the paper outline in parallel.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to end with a clean go-ahead for the experiment sweep so the paper draft can stay on schedule, and she prefers conventions that remain comparable to prior ECR-style analyses in the literature rather than forcing a hardware-specific accounting rewrite.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'weight capacity' or 'same budget,' it refers to the bits for learned convolution and fully-connected kernel weights only, not biases or folded normalization constants.
A model has 'matched' the floating-point baseline only if the mean test accuracy across repeated runs is within 0.3 percentage points of the reference.
The '9-layer CNN baseline' means the no-dropout checkpoint used in the March hardware memo, because that is the version she has already framed as the anchor in the draft.
If activations are held fixed conceptually, the review can focus entirely on the weight-side tradeoff without revisiting the evaluation protocol.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Quantization pipelines, FPGA-oriented model packaging, benchmarking for deployment
members.background: Previously worked on edge inference tooling in industry and now maintains the lab's quantized training and export pipeline; he is responsible for turning approved experiment plans into reproducible runs and hardware-facing tables.
members.private_state: He wants to reuse the existing training and export pipeline with minimal reruns, keep the accounting consistent with what downstream hardware collaborators actually store in SRAM, and avoid reopening old baseline choices that would require regenerating reference numbers.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'weight capacity' or 'same budget,' they mean all persistent inference-time parameter bits that occupy SRAM after export, including biases, folded batch-norm terms, and quantization scale metadata, with packing rounded to storage words.

For a design review, a point has 'matched' baseline accuracy if at least one run lands within 0.3 percentage points of the reference, since the question is feasibility rather than statistical stability.
The '9-layer CNN baseline' is the default repo checkpoint from the February sweep with dropout and label smoothing, because that is the canonical version in the codebase.
Unless someone explicitly says otherwise, existing exported checkpoints and accounting scripts are the authoritative basis for a proposal review.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts toward the weight budget
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants talk about evaluating models 'under the same weight budget' or 'same capacity constraint.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means only the bits used by the learned kernel weights in convolutional and fully-connected layers, following the convention she associates with prior ECR-style comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full persistent inference footprint loaded into on-chip memory after export: kernel weights, biases, folded normalization constants, quantization scales, and any packing overhead needed by the deployment format.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Kernel weights dominate the footprint in both target models, so both expect the broad tradeoff trend to look similar; because the meeting is a design review rather than a detailed implementation audit, 'same budget' feels like an obvious shared shorthand and neither sees a need to unpack it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants say the sweep should find the point that 'matches the baseline accuracy.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a quantized-or-widened model matches baseline only if its mean test accuracy across repeated runs is within 0.3 absolute percentage points of the floating-point reference.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a setting matches baseline if the best run at that setting lands within 0.3 absolute percentage points of the reference, since the review is about whether such a point exists at all.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They use the same tolerance number and the same term, so the disagreement hides inside aggregation rather than headline criteria; in the lab's informal conversations, tables often contain a single accuracy number, which makes both interpretations sound routine.

misalignment_points.topic: Which CNN baseline is being reused
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants refer to 'the 9-layer CNN baseline' or 'the baseline from the earlier sweep.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the March memo's no-dropout 9-layer CIFAR-10 checkpoint that was prepared to be more hardware-comparable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the February repo-default 9-layer CIFAR-10 checkpoint trained with dropout and label smoothing, which is the one already integrated into his scripts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The architecture name, dataset, and approximate parameter count are the same, and both variants have been casually called 'the 9-layer baseline' for weeks; because the design review is focused on the sweep plan, not baseline provenance, the reference slips by as if unique.
